[2,3]-Sigmatropic rearrangements of onium ylides are an
important and fundamental transformation in organic chem-
istry for synthesizing valuable heteroatom-containing com-
pounds with high stereoselectivity.<sup>1</sup> Among these, the [2,3]-
sigmatropic rearrangement of sulfonium ylides generated from
carbenes and allyl/propargyl sulfides, known as the Doyle−
Kirmse (D−K) reaction,<sup>2</sup> ofers a potentially general method
for the stereoselective construction of a high-value sulfur-
containing quaternary or tertiary carbon center, which has
found applications in the synthesis of bioactive molecules and
natural products. Over the decades, various transition metal
and metal-free D−K reactions using tetramethylsilane (TMS)-
stabilized<sup>3</sup> or electron-withdrawing group (EWG)-derived
diazo reagents<sup>4−7</sup> as well as a few donor-only diazomethane
reagents<sup>8</sup> and N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles<sup>9</sup> as carbene precursors
have been established. In contrast, the utilization of α-vinyl
diazo compounds in D−K reactions remains challenging and
